task:
One-line .env fix, but a real ongoing problem: Shivani's forwarded retail mail is STILL flooding Irtiza's personal inbox. NEEDS THIS MACHINE - .env is gitignored.

Verified in his Gmail on 2026-09-17: messages from toozy@inkboxmail.com, each a "Fwd:" of mail originally addressed To: brshivani@gmail.com, arriving on Sep 15 and Sep 16 (SHEIN, Belk, Kendra Scott, MyFitnessPal, cookiedelivery.com, fresh.com, and more). This is exactly the flood Irtiza complained about, and it is still happening.

Root cause: on task b5d09ffe you set OWNER_FORWARD_EXCLUDE_RECIPIENTS but left it BLANK, reporting "left blank per its own documented safe default (no noisy sender identified yet)." That was a misread - the noisy recipient was already identified, and it is the entire reason the variable exists. Read the variable's own comment block in .env.example: it says in as many words that it was added on 2026-09-16 specifically because a candidate's full Gmail-forwarded inbox was flooding OWNER_FORWARD_EMAIL.

Fix: set it to her address.

  OWNER_FORWARD_EXCLUDE_RECIPIENTS=brshivani@gmail.com

That value is not a secret and not personal data in any sense that matters here - it is already committed in this repo's own git history in several places, and it is the literal thing the variable is documented to hold.

Verify afterward, don't just set it and assume:
1. Confirm the running process actually picked up the new value (the webhook/forwarding path reads .env at process start - restart whatever holds it if needed; check the LaunchAgent for the inkbox webhook).
2. Watch for ~15 minutes and confirm no new "Fwd:" messages addressed to brshivani@gmail.com arrive in irtizaa36@gmail.com.
3. Confirm mail genuinely addressed TO the Inkbox mailbox itself still forwards normally - the exclusion matches on the original recipient, so it must not suppress her direct replies to the job-search feedback loop. That distinction is the whole design; breaking it would silently kill the feedback loop.

Report what you set, whether a restart was needed, and the result of all three checks.

macmini.output:
Set OWNER_FORWARD_EXCLUDE_RECIPIENTS=brshivani@gmail.com in .env (previously left blank on task b5d09ffe - that was a misread, the noisy recipient was already known). Restarted com.aiagentsystem.inkbox-webhook (launchctl kickstart -k) so it picked up the new value - confirmed via a fresh PID and the process log showing a clean stop/restart.

All three verification checks passed:
1. Functional test against the live code + live .env (node --env-file=.env -e '...'): mail originally addressed to brshivani@gmail.com correctly returns forward:false; mail addressed directly to the Inkbox mailbox itself (her feedback-loop replies) still returns forward:true. Confirms the fix targets the right thing without breaking the feedback loop.
2. Watched for the full 15 minutes post-restart: baseline was 201 total matching flood emails in Irtiza's Gmail, most recent at 05:03:29Z (a few minutes before the 05:10:17Z restart). Re-checked Gmail after the watch window - zero new ones arrived; the newest is still that same pre-restart message. Flood has stopped.
3. Direct real-world confirmation from the webhook receiver's own log (found while working an unrelated urgent task): the most recent line in .orchestrator/webhook-receiver.log is a live inbound message processed moments after the restart, reading exactly 'forwarding skipped: message was originally addressed to brshivani@gmail.com, which is excluded from owner-forwarding' - the exclusion firing correctly on real production traffic, not just a synthetic test.

Feedback loop unaffected per check 1 and per design (the exclusion matches on original recipient, not on whether it's the Inkbox mailbox's own address).
